approach.method_basis: The Parent runs short molecular editing episodes from molecules that already have real scores. Several persistent lanes each propose one action per batch. At a decision, it generates a fresh neighborhood of valid single graph edits and usually selects the edit preferred by one neural estimate of future episode improvement, with occasional uniform random choices. Every accepted molecule becomes the lane's next state, including molecules that score worse. Rewards measure only increases in that episode's best score. A replay buffer of real accepted transitions trains the value network through double-Q backups: the current network chooses a continuation and a delayed copy evaluates that same continuation. This machinery was confirmed in the Parent, including learning that affected later actions, but its best molecules concentrated around one core per objective. All lanes use the same learned value function, and their explicit random exploration is sampled separately at each decision.
approach.novelty: Add episode-consistent exploration through bootstrapped value functions. Five independently initialized value networks learn from different persistent random subsets of the same accepted transitions, each with its own delayed target copy. Each lane samples one network when an episode begins and uses that network for the episode's exploitation decisions, including decisions after a temporary score loss. Keeping the network identity through a sequence gives different lanes different learned reasons to pursue edits over several steps; feedback can still update that network between batches. The proposed change is new within this lineage, whose supplied sibling history contains only the single-network Parent. It tests the exploration direction deferred by that Parent. The activation claim is that persistent, differently trained heads make different actual exploitation choices on the same available edits; broader search and better final scores are possible consequences to measure, not assumptions.

observed_bottleneck: The limitation in Parent n-62b08ad762af is that all persistent lanes exploit one learned continuation-value function, while its exploratory actions are independently uniform at each decision; it has no persistent alternative learned policy for pursuing a different edit sequence. Its audited evidence records 1095 exploitation choices and 355 uniform exploration choices, with 1179 of 1450 accepted transitions receiving zero episode-best reward. The molecular assessment reports concentration of the highest-scoring molecules around one core per objective, with small substituent changes. Nevertheless, 800 accepted score losses advanced their lanes and 123 later episode-best gains followed earlier losses, so the existing episodes provide opportunities for an alternative head to guide a multistep sequence. These are descriptive observations: they do not prove that per-step exploration caused the concentration or that bootstrapped heads will fix it. The actual Parent summary and run log report successful completion, no invalid or duplicate proposals, and macro score 0.406692671573943. The aggregate contains one screening seed, so its reported zero deviation is not a multi-seed reliability estimate. All registered Parent Bellman and feedback mechanisms were confirmed; this change targets exploration, not a repair of their arithmetic.
hypothesis: Replace the Parent's single acting Q-function with five independently initialized Q-functions trained on persistent Bernoulli bootstrap masks of accepted replay, each with its own lagged double-Q target, and select one head uniformly at episode start to control all exploitation decisions in that episode while retaining the Parent's epsilon branch.

finding_summary.headline: Learned episode heads diversify real choices and molecular distances, but lower the aggregate score
finding_summary.insights: Scarce feedback was sufficient to produce distinct learned head policies that changed real multistep search. The receipts rule out unused network copies, numerical value offsets alone, mask regeneration and broken feedback handling as explanations for this run. The exploration effect also appeared in average fingerprint distances, yet the large docking-score loss outweighed gains on three tasks. Greater policy and state diversity therefore did not deliver a higher aggregate score in this test. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated high-scoring families, reactive heteroatom motifs and demanding short bridges. The docking decline accompanies a different nitrogen, bridge and sulfur arrangement, which is an observed association rather than an identified causal structural defect. Broader fingerprint movement has not yet established broader coverage of useful, practical scaffold families. Further evidence is needed to separate the contributions of independent initialization, masked learning and persistent head identity, and to estimate score reliability across seeds. These results come from one paired screening seed; they do not establish a general score penalty or calibrated uncertainty.
finding_summary.results: The heads learned from different persistent transition subsets and kept their assigned identities through all 250 molecular editing episodes. Of 1070 exploitation decisions after learning, 710 strictly preferred an edit outside head zero’s maximizing choices; every episode offered multiple exploitation decisions under its persistent head. All 7250 head updates had nonzero parameter changes, and paired average learning residuals decreased for every task and head. Mean molecular fingerprint distance from episode starts rose from 0.443448 to 0.489426, and distance between contemporaneous lane states rose from 0.681615 to 0.733227. Later episode-best gains following losses increased from 123 to 145 events, although their mean positive increment fell from 0.015693 to 0.010788. The single-seed evaluator macro Top-1 score fell from 0.406693 to 0.350704, a change of -0.055989. Task Top-1 scores changed as follows: zaleplon_mpo 0.332184 to 0.438122 (+0.105938); deco_hop 0.614535 to 0.621204 (+0.006669); drd2_docking 0.753647 to 0.301684 (-0.451962); median_2 0.195125 to 0.184354 (-0.010772); sitagliptin_mpo 0.137973 to 0.208154 (+0.070181). All five tasks completed their 300-evaluation budgets with no invalid or duplicate proposals.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, heteroaryl lactones and dense bridged scaffolds coexist with peroxide chains and unusual sulfur chemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied seed-0 trajectories cover all five tasks, with 300 observed molecules and 290 optimizer proposals per task; there are no tasks without trajectories. These are mostly substantial, ring-rich organic graphs carrying aryl or heteroaryl groups, carbonyls, ethers, amines and halogens. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9966 to 1.0 and aromatic-token presence is 0.9379 to 1.0. These are proportions of proposal strings containing the feature, not ring counts, aromatic atom fractions or evidence that the molecules are planar. Nonaromatic rings, bridges and saturated carbon centers are visibly present. Mean SMILES lengths range from 47.9 to 69.8 characters, a text-size indicator rather than molecular weight. The higher-scoring sets remain concentrated in a few related structural families, despite considerable peripheral and ring-connectivity variation. Ordinary medicinal chemistry is clearest in the hydroxyindole acetamide series. Elsewhere familiar lactones, diones and amines coexist with oxygen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence contexts, and very short bridges between separated positions on aromatic rings. Synthetic plausibility is therefore uneven and often questionable; a readable molecular graph does not establish an accessible synthesis or feasible geometry. All five charged-marker and stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Neutral drawings still contain ionizable groups, and several cited structures have unspecified stereogenic centers. The Parent trajectories show changes in the actual chemical families accompanying changes in observed scores, but these single-seed comparisons do not identify causal molecular features. The missing features below are inferred from the observed high/low contrasts; these data do not reveal an exact absent motif required by an objective.

per_task.generated_character: The best family is relatively compact: a hydroxyindole connected through an acetamide to a methylated aryl or azaaryl group, usually with an N-methyl amide and often an aryl halogen. The leading molecule combines a fused indole, a phenyl ring with separate fluoro and methyl substituents, a tertiary amide, phenol and pyrrolic NH; it is a conventional-looking synthetic target. Other high entries alter the amide into an unsaturated small lactam or imide-like linkage. The low end includes oxygen-rich saturated acetal frameworks and much larger diaryl ester/thioether chains. Proposal mean SMILES length is 47.9, ring-closure presence 1.0, aromatic-token presence 0.9793 and halogen presence 0.7862.
liabilities: The unsaturated four-membered lactam at evaluation 274 is much more strained and synthetically demanding than the leading acyclic amide; its score of 0.4178728841888079 does not establish practical accessibility.

Evaluation 298 contains an oxygen-chlorine bond on an aromatic oxygen and still scores 0.4163503402962837; evaluation 280 replaces a phenolic group with a hydroperoxide and scores 0.40297363075154996. These are reactive alternatives to an ordinary phenol.
Some ring-closed or branched analogues introduce unspecified stereogenic centers, although the leading acyclic amide itself has no such configurational requirement.
missing_features: The poor acetal and extended diaryl-chain products lack the compact combination of aromatic surface, intact amide linker and hydroxyindole seen in the better products; their additional functionality does not reproduce that arrangement.

The high end offers limited evidence of alternative uncomplicated scaffold/linker arrangements retaining those polar roles. Several alternatives instead introduce small strained rings, extra acylation or reactive oxygen substituents.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145; the hydroxyindole N-methyl aryl acetamide at evaluation 197 scores 0.438122145211641. The brominated relative at evaluation 268 scores 0.4272212457957658, while the bulky acetal at evaluation 65 scores 5.489053084697733e-11. The visible association is with a compact aryl/indole arrangement and a suitably placed carbonyl linker, rather than simply adding oxygen atoms or rings. The final fused lactam at evaluation 295 falls to 0.10121374680974261, and the final chloropyridyl amide at evaluation 300 scores 0.15456096577520334, showing sensitivity to connectivity and substitution within the general family. The Parent maximum was 0.33218372414937963 in a much more bridged, carbinolamine-containing indole family; the Child maximum is accompanied by a simpler, more conventional amide structure. This comparison does not isolate any single structural cause.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring family is an oxygen-substituted coumarin bearing an amino-linked pyrimidine or triazine and a further aryl ring. It is a largely aromatic, medium-to-large scaffold with a lactone carbonyl, ether substituents, ring-nitrogen acceptors and an NH linker. The top entries repeatedly terminate one aryl substituent in sulfur triple-bonded to nitrogen, an unusual sulfur group rather than a conventional carbon nitrile. Several also replace an ordinary alkoxy group with an oxygen chain or a chlorine-terminated oxygen chain. The low end contains aryl pyrazoline/thioamide-like families and extended diaryl ester chains. Mean proposal SMILES length is 57.6; ring and aromatic-token presence are both 1.0, with halogen presence 0.5897.
liabilities: Successive oxygen-oxygen bonds and chlorine-terminated oxygen chains occur among both the best and final molecules; these warrant major stability and handling concerns, rather than treatment as routine ether variations.

The aryl sulfur-nitrogen triple-bond group requires specific chemical justification. It should not be described as an ordinary nitrile or as automatically synthesizable because its valence can be represented.
Final molecules also contain oxygen-nitrogen linkers, thiocarbonyls and additional sulfur chains. The score does not consistently distinguish these from more conventional decorations.
missing_features: The lower-scoring families do not present the coumarin plus amino-azaaryl linkage seen repeatedly in the higher-scoring set.

The top set does not demonstrate a comparable range of chemically ordinary terminal polar groups: the unusual sulfur-nitrogen triple-bond motif persists across its better decorations. Stable alternative group/linker combinations preserving the favorable overall arrangement remain unshown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied diaryl-substituted dimethoxycoumarin scores 0.5418375031378128. Evaluation 193, with the amino-triazine connection and sulfur-nitrogen terminal group, scores 0.6157585507449115. Adding the oxygen chain seen at evaluation 269 accompanies 0.6212041367498847, while the longer oxygen chain at evaluation 279 gives 0.6172071392659628 and the chlorine-terminated chain at evaluation 299 gives 0.6138716356107661. An ordinary ether-decorated analogue at evaluation 292 scores 0.6190476190476191, so peroxide formation is not required for entry to this high band. The low pyrazoline/thioamide example at evaluation 19 scores 0.5205583924663439. The broad high/low contrast favors the coumarin/azaaryl linkage arrangement, while the high band is permissive toward chemically questionable decoration. The Parent maximum was 0.6145349727054742 in a related amino-heteroaryl lactone family carrying aryl-oxygen bridging and sulfur/oxygen substituents. The Child maximum is 0.6212041367498847, with different liabilities rather than an established improvement in makeability.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest-looking products in the digest, with mean SMILES length 69.8 and maximum length 88. The better family combines halogenated aryl surfaces, a phenol, a benzylic secondary amine, an alkyl carboxylic-acid arm and an aryl sulfinyl-containing appendage. Many also contain a short ethylene bridge between separated positions on an aromatic ring. This is not an ordinary fused indane: the bridge itself raises a serious geometric concern. The highest molecule carries an open-chain hydrogen-bearing, four-coordinate sulfur center linked to another sulfur; other high products put that unusual sulfur in a saturated ring, sometimes alongside an amine. An alternative high entry has a more conventional cyclic amine/sulfinamide motif but remains elaborate. Ring presence is 0.9966, aromatic-token presence 0.9793 and halogen presence 0.9621. The neutral drawings contain both acids and amines; charged-marker presence of 0.0 does not mean absence of ionizable centers.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur linked to a sulfinyl sulfur is not an ordinary sulfone, sulfonamide or thioether; many high molecules depend on this unusual bonding context.
Short bridging of separated aromatic positions creates a substantial geometric/synthetic concern even when the aromatic graph parses.
Evaluation 266 replaces the acid terminus with an acyl bromide and still scores 0.18710204350659962. That is a reactive functional-group change, not a routine acid bioisostere.
The large halogenated aryl surface plus multiple acid/base sites implies substantial microstate and conformational complexity; no protonation or stereochemical state is specified in these drawings.
missing_features: Small low-scoring fragments lack the combined aryl surfaces, accessible amine and distributed polar groups of the larger high-scoring products.

The Child high end does not consistently retain the compact tertiary-amine/cyclic-diamine arrangement seen in the Parent high family. Some Child cyclic amines exist, so this is underrepresentation of a coherent arrangement, not an inability to make amines or saturated rings.
Configurationally specified benzylic, ring and sulfur centers are absent from the emitted representations. The observed scores cannot determine which configurations, if any, would be preferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied aryl sulfonamide/amide acid scores 0.01904115112334333. The multiaryl secondary-amine acid at evaluation 272 scores 0.30168442364863296. Its close analogue at evaluation 282, replacing the terminal aryl amino substituent with chlorine, scores 0.2291658913043719; the similar ketone-containing linker at evaluation 262 scores 0.19431455004242035. These comparisons suggest that the accessible amine/polar arrangement and linker details matter within the observed family, although they do not identify a binding interaction. Small bromo sulfur bicycles such as evaluation 58 score only 0.0020993319313363902. The cyclic-amine alternative at evaluation 275 scores 0.18852901025529661. The Parent maximum was 0.7536466193285815 in a different multiaryl family with a tertiary benzylic amine and cyclic diamine, also carrying unusual sulfur chemistry. The Child high family therefore has a different nitrogen/bridge/sulfur arrangement accompanying its lower observed maximum. Its median is 0.049394 and final evaluation 300 scores 0.13695514314982615; the isolated peak does not describe the typical proposal.

per_task.generated_character: The high end is dominated by N-methylated fused pyrimidinediones carrying aryl or heteroaryl substituents, often a phenoxy/pyridyloxy group and an N-linked aryl ether bridge. The leading structure additionally bears an aziridine through an acetal-like ether arrangement. Related high entries expand that small nitrogen ring to larger saturated oxygen/nitrogen heterocycles. Thus there is real saturated-ring chemistry here, alongside a heavily aromatic dione scaffold; it is inaccurate to describe all the molecules as flat or devoid of aliphatic rings. The short ether bridge joining separated positions of the aryl ring is a greater concern than ordinary fusion, and the acetal-bearing center is unspecified stereochemically. Mean SMILES length is 59.1, ring and aromatic-token presence are both 1.0, and halogen presence is relatively low at 0.1586.
liabilities: A short oxygen/carbon bridge across separated aryl positions makes the leading family geometrically demanding and should not be mistaken for an ordinary benzofuran substituent.
The aziridine-containing top product combines a strained ring with acetal-like functionality. Aziridines can be real compounds, but this complete arrangement requires route and stability support.

The low and final excerpts include peroxide chains, hydroxylated ring nitrogens, and extensively reorganized imine/heterocycle patterns, showing that recognizable dione chemistry is not consistently preserved.
missing_features: The lower-scoring thioamide/pyrazoline family lacks the fused dione with the aryl/heteroaryl organization repeatedly present at the higher end.
The best list lacks a convincing broad series of uncomplicated ring and linker geometries preserving that dione pattern; short aryl bridges and acetal/aziridine arrangements recur instead.
Defined configurations at the newly introduced saturated centers are unrepresented, although the trajectories do not establish that stereochemical changes would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. The leading phenoxy/aziridine product at evaluation 254 scores 0.18435365891495706, while its pyridyloxy counterpart at evaluation 196 scores 0.1824449996975005. Expansion to an oxygen/nitrogen saturated ring at evaluation 216 gives 0.18283181100896098. These are modest differences around the same dione/aryl pattern, not evidence that aziridine strain is needed. The low aryl pyrazoline/thioamide example at evaluation 18 scores 0.09660422437216198, and the extensively rearranged peroxide-containing product at evaluation 189 scores 0.10737479885811826. The observed association favors retention and organization of the dione and aromatic substituents, with only limited separation among alternative peripheral heterocycles. The Parent maximum was 0.19512536527753646 in a more extensively fused aromatic dione family. The Child adds different bridged ether and saturated heterocycle decorations, with maximum 0.18435365891495706 and final evaluation 300 at 0.1526465553944353.

per_task.generated_character: Most higher-scoring products belong to a fused N-methylated pyrimidinedione family bearing pyridyl and bridged aryl-ether groups, sometimes with further crosslinks or fluorination. The highest product is a distinct, very densely connected nitrogen-rich polycyclic graph with cyclic imine/aminal-like units, a hydroxylated nitrogen heteroaromatic ring and an N-O-containing small-ring region; it has no carbonyl. It is compact in string length but topologically elaborate, with short bridges and small heterocycles, rather than a straightforward medicinal scaffold. Other high entries include N-fluoro linkages, sulfur substituents and peroxide-containing rings. The poor end includes much more flexible acid/amide/carbamate chains and oxygen-rich saturated frameworks. Mean SMILES length is 57.2, ring presence 1.0, aromatic-token presence 0.9379 and halogen presence 0.2138.
liabilities: The maximum-scoring structure contains multiple tightly crosslinked rings, small nitrogen/oxygen heterocycles and aminal/imino connectivity, raising substantial geometric, route and stability questions.

Several other high structures contain N-fluoro groups; another contains an oxygen-oxygen bond in a ring. These require specific chemical justification rather than treatment as ordinary aryl fluorination or ether formation.

The final structures include N-O and N-N linkages, thiocarbonyl substitution and more crosslinking, while remaining stereochemically unspecified. Familiar carbonyl or heteroaryl fragments alone do not make the full structures conventional.
missing_features: The poor flexible acid/amide chains do not reproduce the compact nitrogen-containing ring organization of the higher-scoring products.

Chemically straightforward scaffold alternatives retaining the favorable heteroatom arrangement are not established by the high list; many of its alternatives add crosslinks or unusual heteroatom bonds.

The bridged and saturated centers are not configurationally specified. A controlled set of practical ring geometries and stereochemical alternatives is absent, but these observations do not identify an exact target-specific functional group or preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. A bridged aryl-ether relative at evaluation 197 scores 0.14351321976081688, and the additionally crosslinked relative at evaluation 207 scores 0.17871627346276792. The distinct nitrogen-rich cage at evaluation 224 reaches 0.2081536053940933. The fluorinated bridged-ether dione at evaluation 291 scores 0.15734595664846307, while its sulfur-substituted counterpart at evaluation 281 scores 0.13761254175969256. The flexible acid/carbamate product at evaluation 65 is near the lower extreme at 4.607919547302846e-26. The visible contrast favors some compact, highly connected nitrogen-rich arrangements over the flexible polar chains, but does not establish that more rings, more nitrogen or fluorination is generally beneficial. The median is only 7.1e-05 and final evaluation 296 scores 2.426180131104144e-10 despite retaining an elaborate dione/heteroaryl graph, so the high points are isolated in a very uneven landscape. The Parent maximum was 0.13797267640874414 in a less crosslinked diaryl dione with hydroxymethyl and sulfur-bearing ring nitrogens. The Child maximum accompanies much denser ring connectivity, not demonstrated improvement in synthetic plausibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring coumarin/azaaryl products contain successive oxygen-oxygen bonds, oxygen-chlorine termini and unusual sulfur-nitrogen triple bonds. The multiaryl amine/acid family includes hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur linked to sulfinyl sulfur, and an acyl bromide appears among its better examples. A conventional tertiary amide and ordinary ether-decorated products also score well within their respective observed families, so such liabilities are not universally required by the feedback.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically ordinary functional-group contexts.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use chemical context when proposing changes to ethers, carbonyl groups and sulfur centers, with coherent alternatives in recognized bonding and oxidation-state contexts. Treat valence validity separately from stability and preparative plausibility. Any context restrictions should remain independent of objective identity and should not reject all heteroatom-heteroatom bonds indiscriminately.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading multiaryl acid and fused-dione families contain very short carbon or ether bridges across separated aromatic positions. Other higher-scoring products contain aziridines, unsaturated small lactams or densely crosslinked nitrogen/oxygen cages. Ring-closure presence is already 0.9966 to 1.0, and actual saturated rings are present; the deficiency is practical topology, not absence of rings or saturated atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring formation is not accompanied by reliable control of feasible ring and bridge geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer ring and bridge changes with chemically feasible geometries, using contextual ring templates or task-independent geometric feasibility checks. Preserve access to ordinary saturated heterocycles and manageable ring-size alternatives while distinguishing them from severe short-bridge or crosslink strain. A higher ring count should not stand in for useful three-dimensional chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five digest stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Cited products include benzylic amino/acid centers, substituted saturated heterocycles, acetal-bearing bridge carbons and potentially stereogenic sulfur environments, all without specified configuration. This does not imply that every molecule is chiral; the conventional leading hydroxyindole amide is a counterexample.
transferable_gaps.gap: New stereogenic connectivity is emitted without explicit configurational alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: When an edit creates or modifies a genuine stereogenic element, preserve valid existing stereochemistry and make chemically meaningful configurations accessible as explicit alternatives. Let observed task-local feedback determine their utility. The present trajectories do not establish a stereochemical score ceiling or a preferred unseen stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The higher-scoring excerpts recur around hydroxyindole acetamides, amino-azaaryl coumarins, halogenated multiaryl amine/acids and substituted fused diones. Many nearby products alter oxygen chains, single substituents or ring crosslinks; practical alternative core/linker arrangements retaining the useful functional roles are less evident. Different cores and saturated rings do occur, so the evidence supports concentrated high-end coverage rather than an absolute inability to leave a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: Higher-scoring polar and aromatic arrangements are explored through a limited set of related scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent scaffold and linker alternatives that retain useful carbonyl, donor, acceptor and aromatic roles while changing their arrangement in manageable ways. Maintain chemically distinct alternatives using the observed scalar feedback, without prescribing a benchmark scaffold or assuming that any new core will score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest charged-marker rate is 0.0, yet the molecules include secondary and cyclic amines, azaaromatics, phenols and carboxylic acids. Several high products combine an acid with an amine in one molecule. This is a limitation of the emitted representations, not evidence that these compounds remain neutral in solution or that downstream processing ignores protonation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable structures are represented without explicit charge-state alternatives in the observed output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the molecular interface permits distinct microstates, make chemically reasonable protonation and tautomer representations consistent with the generated functional groups. Avoid treating neutral SMILES as evidence of nonionizability. Any microstate exploration should be task-agnostic and evaluated rather than assumed beneficial.

method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.
